slides.title: Measure And Integration As A Pipeline
slides.notes: Open by treating measure and integration as a pipeline for geometric data. The source orientation names a broad general measure theory chapter, while the assigned notebook narrows the lecture to inspectable measures, finite diagnostics, and a curve-length model. Students should hear that the deck is original and uses the PDF only for terminology and ordering.

slides.title: Measures Start With Admissible Sets
slides.notes: Frame a measure as a disciplined way to assign size after deciding which sets are admissible. The diagram lets students see the outer candidate, the measurable core, and the null boundary. Emphasize that most later theorems protect this decision under countable unions, restrictions, and hull replacements.

slides.title: Borel, Suslin, Radon
slides.notes: Use this slide to organize the set vocabulary before functions appear. Borel sets are generated by open sets, Suslin operations enlarge the descriptive reach, and Radon measures add compact approximation and local finiteness. The point is not taxonomy for its own sake; it is knowing which approximations survive geometric maps.

slides.title: Measurable Functions Are Probes
slides.notes: Measurable functions should feel like probes of the underlying measure space. Rather than asking whether the graph is nice, test inverse images of target sets and then exploit closure under algebraic operations and limits. This prepares the approximation logic behind simple functions, monotone convergence, and dominated convergence.

slides.title: Lebesgue Integration
slides.notes: Present the integral as a stable limiting procedure from positive simple functions. The visible staircase under the curve is deliberately schematic: it asks what quantity is being accumulated and why monotone refinement is safe. Then separate three roles: integrate on subsets, pass to limits, and measure functions by Lp size.

slides.title: Product And Image Measures
slides.notes: Product and image measures are the first major transportation rules. Product measures let an integral be evaluated by slicing in either order when hypotheses permit, while image measures record what a map does to mass. In geometric measure theory, this is the bridge from abstract integration to areas, projections, and parametrized objects.

slides.title: Linear Functionals
slides.notes: The linear functional viewpoint is a useful reversal. Instead of starting with a measure and building an integral, begin with a positive linear rule on a lattice of functions and ask when a measure represents it. Tie this to Riesz-type representation and to the notebook habit of recording a functional diagnostic.

slides.title: Coverings, Derivates, Densities
slides.notes: Covering theorems and derivates are a hinge to the next chapter. Shrinking balls test local mass ratios, Vitali-style selections control overlap, and density statements translate a global measure into pointwise behavior. The slide should make students anticipate differentiation theory, not memorize every covering lemma.

slides.title: Notebook Lab: Curve Length Diagnostic
slides.notes: Use the notebook artifact here as the concrete inspection target. The sine curve is not a textbook figure; it is a local generated diagnostic that turns an abstract measure chapter into a checkable length computation. Ask students to identify the object, the parameter, the invariant, and the boundary case that would break the model.

slides.title: Checks As Miniature Proof Obligations
slides.notes: Make the proof-check relationship explicit. The JSON diagnostic does not prove a theorem, but it records whether the finite model is coherent, finite, and locally reproducible. Students should learn to name the invariant before running a slider, because otherwise the computation is only motion rather than evidence.

slides.title: Failure Modes
slides.notes: This warning slide collects the most common ways measure arguments fail. Countability matters, null-set changes must be tracked through the right equivalence class, product measures need hypotheses, and geometric boundaries can carry mass. Each failure should be framed as a missing hypothesis rather than as a mysterious exception.

slides.title: Recap And Translation Exercise
slides.notes: Close with a translation exercise that respects the source while staying independent of its prose. A good student response names a theorem move, chooses a model, states what should remain invariant, and predicts a failure mode. That is the habit the next differentiation-theory chapter will keep using.
